summary: This bill updates the federal poverty line calculation by requiring the Secretary of Health and Human Services to annually revise it based on a comprehensive set of household expenditures, including food, housing, childcare, and healthcare costs, adjusted for inflation and regional variations, and to publish these revised poverty lines for different household sizes and geographic areas.

scores.thoughts: This bill directly aims to update the federal poverty line calculation to expand eligibility for and utilization of federal assistance and benefits. By redefining poverty to include more accurate costs of basic needs, regional variations, and changing spending norms, it would inherently make more people eligible for social safety net programs, thus expanding welfare.

By revising the poverty line upward to reflect more realistic costs of basic needs (including health care), the bill expands eligibility for numerous federal means-tested programs, which will increase mandatory spending and thereby enlarge the deficit. The effect is real but secondary; the bill itself contains no appropriations or deficit-reduction language and is not framed as a fiscal measure.

The new poverty-line formula explicitly incorporates ACA benchmark premiums, Medicare Advantage drug-plan premiums, and median out-of-pocket medical costs, thereby raising the income threshold for programs that subsidize health coverage. This constitutes a government-driven expansion of eligibility rather than a market-oriented approach, though health care is only one of several cost components in the revised measure.
